items.title: Ray Vega interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 20, 2023
items.q: Another one of our buds in those circles was David Glasser who plays lead alto with the Basie band.

ctx.x: together for these Blue Note sessions which they really just — these were not working bands. They got together, looked at the music and went in. But at that point they were speaking to each other in such a highly sophisticated fashion that they could hear through things. They could hear through things. So what I tell the students is I tell them you’re not going to be able to play freely if all you’re going to have is that piece of music in front of you and looking at the chord progressions to figure out what you…

remember going down to 24th Street and they had an interesting loft apartment, it was a great apartment. I remember getting up there and he had like an old school stereo system, you know a real nice sounding stereo, and he’d put that recording on of Dexter Gordon’s “Sophisticated Giant” and we just sat there, Pablo and myself I think. Pablo Carey teaches in Maine. Another one of our buds in those circles was David Glasser who plays lead alto with the Basie band. So we’d be sitting there going oh wow, and…

I’ve insisted that there’s a magic to improvisation, to jazz improvisation that’s not really explainable but that is a problem I think in the world of education because you can’t teach a four year program on jazz without getting into the codifying of it. I mean how are you going to adjust —
